title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description:
A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes in the sequence has an edge connecting them. A node can only appear in the sequence at most once. Note that the path does not need to pass through the root.

The path sum of a path is the sum of the node's values in the path.

Given the root of a binary tree, return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path. Node values may be negative.

examples.explanation: The optimal path is 2 -> 1 -> 3 with a path sum of 2 + 1 + 3 = 6.
The optimal path is 15 -> 20 -> 7 with a path sum of 15 + 20 + 7 = 42.
A single node is the only path, so its value is the answer.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 3 * 10^4].
approach: Run a postorder DFS that returns the maximum downward gain each node can contribute to its parent: the node's value plus the larger of its two child gains, with child gains clamped at zero so harmful branches are dropped. While recursing, a full path may bend through a node and use both children, so at each node update a global maximum with node.val plus both (clamped) child gains. Because the global answer starts at negative infinity and the bending candidate always includes at least one node's value, all-negative trees are handled correctly. Each node is visited once, giving O(n) time and O(h) recursion space for tree height h.
